findings.problem: The solution requires the triangle angle-sum rule. The lesson teaches the right angle opposite a diameter but does not teach the angle-sum rule or name it as a prerequisite.
findings.fix: Teach the triangle angle-sum rule or name the lesson that teaches it as a prerequisite.

findings.problem: The question requires opposite angles of an inscribed quadrilateral to sum to 180 degrees. The lesson does not teach this rule or point to a prerequisite that does.
findings.fix: Add the cyclic-quadrilateral angle rule and a worked example to the lesson.

findings.problem: The question requires the angle between intersecting chords to equal half the sum of the intercepted arcs. The lesson teaches intersecting-chord length products but does not teach this angle rule or name a prerequisite.
findings.fix: Teach the intersecting-chords angle rule with a worked example.

findings.problem: The question requires the external-secant angle rule, half the difference of the intercepted arcs. The lesson teaches secant length products but does not teach this angle rule or name a prerequisite.
findings.fix: Teach the external-secant angle rule and identify the far and near arcs in an example.

findings.problem: The solution requires the diagonal and area properties of an inscribed square. The lesson does not teach these properties or point to a prerequisite covering them.
findings.fix: Add an inscribed-square example that establishes the diagonal as the diameter and finds the square's area.

findings.problem: The solution requires the 30-60-90 triangle rule that the side opposite 30 degrees is half the hypotenuse. The lesson does not teach this rule or name it as a prerequisite.
findings.fix: Teach the 30-60-90 side relationship or name the lesson that teaches it as a prerequisite.
